# Love Me Forever (Pinkshift album)
Love Me Forever is the debut studio album by American rock band Pinkshift. It was released on October 21, 2022, through Hopeless Records. The album, produced by veteran punk engineer Will Yip, showcases Pinkshift’s blend of pop-punk, punk rock and post-hardcore influences with elements of grunge. Its 12 tracks channel raw emotion and social frustration, supported by a high-energy sound and Ashrita Kumar’s powerful vocals. Love Me Forever was met with positive reviews from music critics, who praised its intense energy and heartfelt songwriting. It was highlighted in several publications’ year-end lists, with Alternative Press calling it “an impeccable debut”, and Kerrang! ranking it among the 50 best albums of 2022.
## Background and Recording
Pinkshift formed in 2018 in Baltimore, Maryland, and built an early following through a string of singles and tours with bands like Pup and Mannequin Pussy. After releasing the Saccharine EP in 2021, the trio began working on their first full-length album. Singer Ashrita Kumar, guitarist Paul Vallejo, and drummer Myron Houngbedji put aside their original plans (such as attending medical and engineering school) to focus on the band. In 2021–2022, Pinkshift signed with Hopeless Records, a label known for pop-punk acts. They recorded Love Me Forever in early 2022 with producer Will Yip, known for his work with bands like Turnstile and The Wonder Years. According to the band, the album sessions captured a “full force and fury,” as they aimed to deliver passionate, unapologetic punk songs with a message.
## Release and Promotion
On June 1, 2022, Pinkshift debuted the album’s first single, “Nothing (In My Head)”, coinciding with the announcement of their signing to Hopeless Records. This track introduced the band’s raucous pop-punk style to a wider audience. The album itself was officially announced on July 14, 2022, alongside the release of the second single “I’m Not Crying, You’re Crying.” That song — which opens the album — was accompanied by a lyric video and described by Kumar as a burst of “raw and unfiltered emotion” kicking off the record with “panicked denial”. In late August 2022, Pinkshift released “Get Out” as the third preview track from Love Me Forever, a fast, thrashing punk anthem. During live shows that summer, the band dedicated “Get Out” to protesting the U.S. Supreme Court’s curtailing of rights, as the song is, in Kumar’s words, “a blatant attack against the white supremacist and patriarchal colonizers of our bodies, homes, and ways of life”. Each single was accompanied by a music video or visualizer, generating buzz in the punk/alternative music scene.
Love Me Forever was released in full on October 21, 2022. To promote the album, Pinkshift embarked on a North American tour in the fall of 2022. The tour kicked off with an album release show in their hometown of Baltimore on October 20, 2022, and continued through early December with dates across the U.S. and Canada. The band’s energetic live performances and the album’s growing critical acclaim helped solidify Pinkshift as a notable new act in punk rock by the end of 2022.
## Music and Lyrics
Musically, Love Me Forever is rooted in pop-punk but frequently pushes into heavier and darker territory. Reviewers noted the album’s “mix of punk, post-hardcore, grunge, and pop” influences, which coalesce into what one critic called “a stunning burst of influences and experiences” fueled by anger. Fast, aggressive rhythms and whirlwind guitar riffs drive many songs, while Kumar’s vocals range from melodic hooks to outright screams. Kerrang! wrote that Pinkshift combines “sugar-rush melody and electric energy” with moments that verge on hardcore aggression, showcasing a versatility beyond typical pop-punk conventions. The production by Will Yip was praised for its clarity and punch, giving the band a sharp, cathartic sound without diluting its raw edge.
Lyrically, the album balances deeply personal themes with broader social commentary. Several tracks explore mental health, heartbreak, and trauma from a first-person perspective. For example, the song “Trust Fall” addresses the emotional fallout of an abusive relationship, laying bare feelings of insecurity and loss of self. On “I’m Not Crying, You’re Crying,” the narrator frantically denies their pain when asked “are you okay?”, an opening that immediately sets a tone of turmoil and vulnerability. “Cherry (We’re All Gonna Die)”, despite its upbeat tempo, carries an ironic nihilism about impending doom. The track “The Kids Aren’t Alright” bluntly voices generational anxiety about the future (at one point observing that “the world is ending all the time”), reflecting young people’s despair amid constant crises.
Other songs turn their focus outward to critique social injustices. “Burn the Witch” reimagines historical witch trials to comment on modern groupthink and misogyny, condemning how society can demonize women. In its chorus, Kumar pointedly challenges listeners with the line, “You’ve got two feet, now won’t you stand for something?”. “Get Out” is an overtly political track; Kumar has described it as an anthem demanding space and autonomy, born from pure “unapologetic rage” against oppressive forces. The title track, “Love Me Forever,” along with the closing acoustic-inflected song “Dreamer,” bring a more introspective angle. Kumar explained that the album’s title encapsulates a plea for unconditional self-acceptance – to “love me forever” even in moments of anger and sadness, as one must learn to love oneself fully in order to persevere. This theme of finding empowerment in one’s own vulnerability ties the album together, even as it traverses from fury to hope.
Despite the often heavy subject matter, Love Me Forever interjects breathing room and dynamics. Mid-album, “In a Breath” stands out as a gentle piano-driven ballad that provides a moment of quiet reflection. Its inclusion highlights the band’s willingness to strip back the noise and reveal a fragile side before launching back into the high-octane finale. Overall, the album’s songwriting toggles between defiance and despair, but ultimately delivers a message of resilience. As one reviewer observed, Pinkshift “walk [the] fraying edge between frenzied confessions and righteous fury” throughout Love Me Forever, yet emerge “unbowed, unbroken, and powerful” by the record’s end.
## Critical Reception
Love Me Forever received generally positive reviews from critics, especially within the punk and alternative rock press. Nick Ruskell of Kerrang! awarded the album a 4 out of 5 rating, praising it as “a bold first proper kick from a band already brimming with promise.” He wrote that the record is accomplished and “wise beyond [the band’s] years,” delivering an infectious one-two punch with its opening tracks and maintaining that momentum throughout. Kerrang! highlighted Pinkshift’s ability to incorporate hardcore influences – noting, for instance, that songs like “Cherry (We’re All Gonna Die)” hit with a Turnstile-like intensity – while still crafting big hooks and energetic punk anthems.
In Flood Magazine, Mischa Pearlman hailed Love Me Forever as a standout debut. He described the album as “a stunning burst of influences and experiences, all of which coalesce in a swirling swathe of anger and injustice”, yet underscored by genuine vulnerability. Pearlman noted the significance of Pinkshift’s perspective as people of color in a scene often dominated by white male voices, calling the album “phenomenal” and “utterly indispensable” for how it channels personal and political rage into cathartic music. Under the Radar magazine’s Caleb Campbell also lauded the record, giving it a score of 7.5 out of 10. Campbell wrote that Pinkshift “conjure the cathartic magic of punk” on a collection of songs that explore “the nihilism of a generation growing up with an uncertain future, the wounds of trauma and abuse, and the alienation of living unapologetically in a hostile world.” Despite these heavy themes, he concluded that the band emerges “unbroken, and powerful,” delivering a “stellar punk debut” that positions Pinkshift among the next generation of the genre.
Several publications cited Love Me Forever as one of the notable rock albums of 2022. Alternative Press included the album in its list of “the 55 best albums of 2022,” praising its “honest lyrics, fast punk beats, and shredding guitars” and calling Love Me Forever “an impeccable debut” for the band. Kerrang! ranked it at No. 19 on their year-end list of the top 50 albums of 2022, a strong endorsement given the magazine’s international profile in rock music. The album also appeared on year-end lists from several niche music sites and critics; for example, The Alternative and Chorus.fm both placed Love Me Forever in their top albums of 2022. Critics commonly noted that beyond the hype of Pinkshift’s early viral success, the album fulfilled and solidified the band’s potential. Consequence (which featured Pinkshift as an “Artist to Watch” in October 2022) commended Love Me Forever as “pop punk for the end of the world,” highlighting the way the record’s urgent riffs and sincere fury captured the mood of a turbulent era.
In summary, Love Me Forever established Pinkshift as a fresh and formidable voice in modern punk. Reviewers praised the album’s balance of visceral punk aggression and emotional authenticity, as well as Pinkshift’s efforts to push for inclusivity in their genre. From its blistering guitar-driven tracks to its moments of melodic release, the album was received as a confident debut that fulfilled the band’s promise and left many excited for what Pinkshift would do next.

Baltimore rock band Pinkshift— composed of vocalist Ashrita Kumar (they/them),  guitarist Paul Vallejo (he/him), and drummer Myron Houngbedji (he/him)—    is releasing their highly anticipated debut album _Love Me Forever_ on October 21st via Hopeless Records. The record sees the band channeling rage while maintaining an early 2000s pop-punk sound. Known for lead singles “Love Me Forever” and “nothing (in my head)” as well as the acoustic tune “In A Breath”, the grunge-tinged and pit-heavy record sees the band standing up to subjugation and oppression while examining the human condition over the course of twelve blistering tracks. The record continues the group’s unapologetic dedication to delivering compelling messages and pushing for POC bands to take up space in a predominantly white rock scene.

Formed in 2018, Pinkshift lined their path to success through a string of critically acclaimed singles and tours with bands such as PUP and Mannequin Pussy across North America and the UK. Kumar eschewed plans to pursue medical school and chemical engineering to pursue music full-time, resulting in the creation of an inventive and exciting band that’s making a mark on a new generation of emo kids. The forthcoming debut album was recorded by Will Yip and is an album laced with fury.

Like their lyrics, the band demands to be heard, unleashing their passion in songs such as [“Burn The Witch”](https://youtu.be/LPA20jgALx8) and ” [Dreamer”](https://youtu.be/bXXQbF3c4gQ), a powerful closer. According to Kumar, “Burn The Witch” comes from a time when they were personally crucified. “I was captain of a dance team in college and one week while I was out sick, there was an insecure team member who took advantage of that situation to oust me of that position and started spreading lies about me. Many of those members felt like family and it was wild to see them turn against me one by one rallying around someone with so much insecurity so if I’m being honest that’s what inspired the rage on the track. Instrumentally we tried to match that rage as close as we could.”

Kumar believes that making the rock scene a space that welcomes POC is an important goal, one that the industry has needed for a long time, and something that they see is slowly becoming more commonplace. “There are definitely more POC bands getting the recognition they deserve like [Meet Me @ The Altar](https://youtu.be/-px9MYLIhGo) and [Magnolia Park](https://youtu.be/TDE6LDaP5z8). I think that’s really cool and hope to see more of that in the future, especially because on the local level there are a lot of additional POC bands that are still smaller and deserve that recognition as well. These are encouraging steps but there still needs to be more work done to have the scene on a national level represent what we see locally.”

Where the start and middle are full of passion, the end of the record swirls with dance-ready vibes. Inspired by the Arctic Monkeys, “Dreamer” is a groovy acoustic track that started off with a riff. ” We wanted something that people could dance to – I remember we were in the practice room and Myron was playing a groove and it started off as a freestyle jam, we structured it from there together. The lyrics started as an acoustic track that I had been working on which paired really well with that groove all fleshed out.”

For Kumar, the album is about more than pushing back against one’s oppressors. “This album is about embracing yourself and everything that comes with it including the anger and sadness, that’s why it’s called Love Me Forever. Love me forever in that anger and sadness and see me through for my triumphant moments. I think that’s an important part of growing and realizing that no one is going to love you more than you love yourself. Expecting to feel loved when you don’t love yourself is not going to work, the album is about going through that and figuring it out.”

![Image 1](https://newnoisemagazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Pinkshift-General-4-Leigh-Ann-Rodgers-240x300.jpg)

Press Photo of Pink shift  
(Credit: Leigh-Ann Rodgers)

With this album, Pinkshift is ready to reclaim punk rock and make it their own for their generation, changing the genre’s narrative one song at a time. The band is on tour in support of the album, starting off in their hometown of Baltimore on October 20th and playing throughout North America until December 6th.

A mix of punk, post-hardcore, grunge, and pop, the Baltimore trio’s debut is a stunning burst of influences and experiences coalescing in a swirling swathe of anger and injustice.

**Pinkshift**  
**_Love Me Forever_**  
**HOPELESS**

Even if you know nothing about its various scenes, you could probably guess that there’s long been a dearth of people of color in alternative rock—and any subgenres thereof. Thankfully, bit by bit, that’s changing, and Baltimore trio [**Pinkshift**](https://pinkshift.bandcamp.com/) are very much at the forefront of that movement. Signed to pop-punk heavyweights Hopeless Records, the trio are smack bang in the middle of a scene infamous for its dominant white-male perspective. They fit in perfectly, while also shaking things up drastically. _Love Me Forever_ is the band’s debut album, which arrives after last year’s _Saccharine_ EP. Like that release, these 12 songs bristle with raw personal emotion, all within the context of the greater world at large and the various systems in place that have held people of color back—particularly in America—for centuries.

That’s all conveyed through lyrics about anxiety, depression, insecurity, and heartbreak—to name just a few of the subjects that vocalist Ashrita Kumar tackles across the album. Whether they’re spitting out rageful defiance, as on blistering opener “i’m not crying you’re crying,” or unconvincing, ironic affirmations as on “cherry (we’re all gonna die),” the vocalist packs generations of trauma into their voice, but channels them into their own specific experiences. It’s the same with the sneering animosity of “Trust Fall” (“I really hate you,” Kumar sings over an urgent melody courtesy of guitarist Paul Vallejo and drummer Myron Houngbedji, “but you’re just a mirror of the past”), the breakneck blast of “BURN THE WITCH,” and the stirring riffs of “Cinderella.”

A mix of punk, post-hardcore, grunge, as well as pop—at times, there are undeniable nods to No Doubt at their most visceral here—_Love Me Forever_ is a stunning burst of influences and experiences, all of which coalesce in a swirling swathe of anger and injustice, not least on brutal penultimate track “let me drown.” Yet beneath it all, there’s also a real vulnerability, too. Just listen to the lyrics of the title track, or if that’s not obvious enough, “in a breath”—the gentle but powerful piano ballad that slows everything down right in the middle of the record. Regardless of the statement it makes within a racially homogenized scene, this is a phenomenal album. Taking that into account makes it utterly indispensable.

Music Theatre Newsletter Get all the top news & discounts for Music & beyond. ✨ Sign Up The Baltimore-based trio - Ashrita Kumar (vocals, they/them), Paul Vallejo (guitar, he/him), Myron Houngbedji (drums, he/him) - have been making their mark both in the U.S. and across the pond since forming in 2018, thanks to a string of critically acclaimed singles, and tours with the likes of PUP and Mannequin Pussy. They eschewed plans for medical school and chemical engineering to pursue music, deliver powerful messages, and show fellow POC artists that they can and should take up space in a predominantly white music scene, and the result is one of the most inventive bands in the punk scene today. Today Pinkshift announce their long-awaited debut album Love Me Forever, out October 21st via Hopeless Records. The LP was recorded by Will Yip (Turnstile, Mannequin Pussy, The Wonder Years, Circa Survive, Tigers Jaw) and over the course of its' 12 blistering songs, Love Me Forever completely unleashes the full force and fury of the band. Following last month's release of "nothing (in my head)," which exemplified the band's agility as they walk the line between riot grrl, punk rock, and post-hardcore, Pinkshift share a new single today entitled "i'm not crying, you're crying." Featuring a rush of guitars and drums, accelerating into a frenzy of raw, ragged emotion, "i'm not crying, you're crying" is a breakneck journey into the heart, soul and mind of a band that, clearly, have a lot to get off their chest, and who do so just as viscerally as they do emotionally. "'crying' is the one song on the record that I didn't start with a particular direction, just raw and unfiltered emotion," explains Kumar. "As the first song on Love Me Forever, it kicks the record off with a panicked denial - an immediately attacking response to the question of "are you okay?" untrusting and doubtful of the intent and sincerity of that question." The 55 best albums of 2022
==========================

[Alternative Press Magazine](https://www.altpress.com/author/alternative-press-magazine/)

|

[December 12, 2022](https://www.altpress.com/2022/12/12)

   ![Image 2: best albums 2022](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/styles/article-hero/2022/12/07/attachment-Collage-Maker-13-Dec-2022-02.16-PM.jpg.webp?t=6392ab00.webp)

*   [SHARE](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https://www.altpress.com/best-albums-2022/ "SHARE")
*   [TWEET](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=The%2055%20best%20albums%20of%202022%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.altpress.com%2Fbest-albums-2022%2F%20%40altpress "TWEET")

In 2022, pop mavens, rap greats, and rock favorites returned, select indie acts broke out to the masses, the pop-punk resurgence continued to thrive, and many upstarts won over the hearts of new fans. All in all: It was a pretty great year for new music. To reflect on the year, like the huge music fans that we are, AltPress rounded up the 55 best albums of 2022. Below, find our favorite records we’ve had on repeat all year, from beloved pop and indie records to hardcore hits and standout hip-hop releases, and everything in between.

The Best Albums of 2022
-----------------------

![Image 3: being funny in a foreign language](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-the-1975-dirty-hit.jpeg)

Dirty Hit

The 1975 – _Being Funny in a Foreign Language_

On their 2019 album, [**the 1975**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/the-1975/) sang about how "sincerity is scary." On this year's release, frontman/lyricist Matty Healy poured out of his heart every feeling he has about allowing oneself to be sincere, giving yourself over to love, and what masculinity means in this day and age. In the most 1975 way possible, that comes across in playful, snarky witticisms and shameless admissions ("Part of the Band," "The 1975," "When We Are Together"), and damn perfect pop songs ("Happiness," "Oh Caroline," "I'm In Love With You") that capture the effervescent feeling of love in sheeny guitars and synths. With each verse that makes you stop in your tracks to either laugh or tear up, you'll feel a little more sincere, too. —_Sadie Bell_

![Image 4: alex g record](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-alex-g-domino.jpeg)

Domino Records

Alex G – _God Save the Animals_

[**Alex G**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/alex-g/)’s ninth studio album, _God Save the Animals_, is further proof that he's the Brian Wilson of the millennial generation. The 13-track release finds him once again covering considerable sonic ground, from introspective folk, hyperpop, emo, and ‘90s alt rock that almost feels cinematic in scope. Whether he's modulating and pitch-shifting his voice or stripping his arrangements down to their bare bones, Alex G’s music is as beautiful as it is unsettling. Even when he ventures into strictly instrumental territory with tracks like “S.D.O.S,” he still conveys so much emotion and meaning. _God Save the Animals_ is Alex G at peak form — defying any creative limitations in pursuit of constant exploration. —_Alessandro DeCaro_ 

![Image 5: alexisonfire album](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-alexisonfire-dine-alone-records.jpeg)

Dine Alone Records

Alexisonfire – _Otherness_

It’s rare for a band to come back in style after 13 years and release their best work to date, but Canadian rock veterans [**Alexisonfire**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/alexisonfire/) did just that. _Otherness_ is proof that sometimes you need to go back to basics to discover who you really are. The LP contains elements of the band’s classic post-hardcore sound, but with a more raw, organic approach that toes the line between classic rock and atmospheric psych-rock — along with three distinct vocalists — to create a sound that could be their own genre at this point. Upon first listen, it's clear that Alexisonfire are firing on all cylinders, sounding more in sync as collaborators and more confident than ever before. —_AD_ 

![Image 6: blue rev](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-blue-rev-polyvinyl-and-transgressive.jpeg)

Polyvinyl / Transgressive

Alvvays – _Blue Rev_

Canada's [**Alvvays**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/alvvays/) tend to take quite a few years between records — and that might just be because every time, they cook up nothing less than indie-pop perfection. Named after the Canadian alcoholic beverage Rev, [_Blue Rev_](https://www.altpress.com/alvvays-blue-rev-interview/) is bubbly and intoxicating, with its shoegaze and power-pop guitars, and varied — at times dreamy and others warped — production. One sip of singer Molly Rankin's poetic musings about heartbreak and growing older and you'll be buzzed on the sheer dreaminess that is _Blue Rev_. _—SB_

![Image 7: architects album](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-architects-epitaph.jpeg)

Epitaph

Architects – _the classic symptoms of a broken spirit_

[**Architects**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/architects/) have consistently been the precursor for what British heavy metal sounds like; they write a riff, and five years later, it’s the only thing you hear on the radio or live. Their 10th studio album is no different, offering the similar themes of nihilism and existentialism you know of the band, but with an optimistic, lively approach. Experimenting with makeup and fashion in music videos, seamlessly blending technical metal verses with pop choruses, Architects still find their artistic challenges to overcome with this release — and in doing so, help to elevate British heavy metal to a mainstream level. —_Yasmine Summan_

![Image 8: the car arctic monkeys](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-arctic-monkeys-domino.jpeg)

Domino Records

Arctic Monkeys – _The Car_

Just when you thought [**Arctic Monkeys**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/arctic-monkeys/) couldn't get more stylish, the English indie titans do the damn thing. On their 2018 record, _Tranquility Base Hotel & Casino_, frontman [Alex Turner](https://www.altpress.com/arctic-monkeys-the-car-interview/) positioned himself and the band as a lounge-pop act rather than one of the biggest rock groups in the world. Here, they keep up the act, but in a way that somehow exudes even more glamor. It sounds pristine, and the sexy, funky moments beg to be heard beneath "a mirrorball." As Turner sings in falsetto about fame, love, and heartbreak over cinematic tracks, they paint a world of panache you can't help but get lost in — much like a vintage romance (perhaps specifically one that plays out in a '70s club that's drenched in velvet). _—SB_

![Image 9: avril love sux](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-avril-dta-and-elektra-records.jpeg)

DTA / Elektra Records

Avril Lavigne – _Love Sux_

The pop-punk revival has dominated the early 2020s, with comebacks from industry mainstays, paired with exciting new artists bursting through the seams. It could arguably feel impossible for acts to break through all the nostalgic noise — but for the reigning pop-punk princess [**Avril Lavigne**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/avril-lavigne/), it’s no sweat. [_Love Sux_](https://www.altpress.com/avril-lavigne-mark-hoppus-after-school-radio-interview/) is like the cooler older sister to 2007's _The Best Damn Thing_, touching on similar topics from a matured perspective, with a strong experience in the field, and more to deliver. And yet, it still manages to connect with the younger crowds, offering collaborations with Machine Gun Kelly and YUNGBLUD. Grammy snub or not, _Love Sux_ should be praised in pop-punk history. —_YS_

![Image 10: un verano sin ti](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-bad-bunny-rimas.jpeg)

RIMAS

Bad Bunny – _Un Verano Sin Tí_

Puerto Rico’s gift to the world has bottled summer and its intricacies in a cross-genre affair that spans dream pop, grimy dembow, merengue, house, and trap. This masterclass in Latin alternative features assists from fellow Boricuas the Marías and Buscabulla, and Colombia’s Bomba Estéreo. [**Bad Bunny**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/bad-bunny/)’s latest proves the future of popular music (in any language) lies in the alternative approach. —_E.R. Pulgar_

![Image 11: bad omens record](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-bad-omens-sumerian-records.jpeg)

Sumerian Records

Bad Omens – _THE DEATH OF PEACE OF MIND_

For their third studio album, [_THE DEATH OF PEACE OF MIND_](https://www.altpress.com/bad-omens-interview-the-death-of-peace-of-mind-issue-403/), [**Bad Omens**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/bad-omens/) made a conscious effort to prove that they are so much more than a metalcore band, and it certainly shows. From the opener “CONCRETE JUNGLE,” which blends moody synths pads, dance beats, and R&B-esque vocals in the vein of Post Malone or the Weeknd to the radio-ready rock anthem “Nowhere To Go,” Bad Omens make every track feel like its own entity while still retaining cohesion. Those who love their heavier material will be satiated just fine with “Artificial Suicide” and “IDWT$,” where the band flex their aggression in compelling new ways. Ultimaely, _THE DEATH OF PEACE OF MIND_ is a record that redefines experimentation in modern metalcore_._ —_AD_

![Image 12: Bartees Strange album](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-bartees-4ad.jpeg)

4AD

Bartees Strange – _Farm To Table_

Ever since his debut, [**Bartees Strange**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/bartees-strange/) has propped the door open to another galaxy. It’s one that seems to stretch infinitely, with possibility and experimentation reigning supreme. On his sophomore album, [_Farm To Table_](https://www.altpress.com/bartees-strange-farm-to-table-interview/), he continues to subvert and challenge how people think about music, from the indie-trap of “Cosigns” to the exuberant dance-pop of “Wretched.” Strange has undergone a momentous year, the type that’s joyful to witness from an artist who continues to evolve and enrapture through sheer curiosity. —_Neville Hardman_

![Image 13: renaissance](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-bey-parkwood-entertainment.jpeg)

Parkwood Entertainment

Beyoncé – _Renaissance_

The disco reverbs, electronic funk breakdowns, and vogue beats are turned to 100 on [**Beyoncé**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/beyonce/)’s latest knockout. _Renaissance_ is a study of nightlife’s queer fringe, featuring samples from legends like Donna Summer and Robin S., production by Chicago house icon Honey Dijon, and appearances from Grace Jones and Big Freedia. Virgo’s groove indeed. —_ERP_ 

![Image 14: beatopia](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-bea-dirty-hit.jpeg)

Dirty Hit

beabadoobee – _Beatopia_

While [**beabadoobee**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/beabadoobee/)'s 2020 debut _Fake It Flowers_ was rife with grunge and the teen angst of a coming-of-age soundtrack, Bea Kristi's sound became more expansive in this year's follow-up [_Beatopia_](https://www.altpress.com/beabadoobee-interview-issue-401/). Less concerned with genre, the Filipina-British singer toys with fizzy guitar-pop and string-flanked ballads with less of a focus on wooing fans with catchy hooks. Instead, _Beatopia_ finds Kristi more confident in experimentation and less worried about fitting into a nostalgic box. —_Ilana Kaplan_

![Image 15: black thought and danger mouse record](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-danger-mouse-bertelsmann-music-group.jpeg)

Bertelsmann Music Group

Black Thought and Danger Mouse – _Cheat Codes_

Since his days swapping bars with Malik B. in the Roots, [**Black Thought**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/black-thought/) has been a consistently great rapper. With _Cheat Codes_, the collaborative album between the visionary MC and producer [**Danger Mouse**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/danger-mouse/), his indelible command is being put in a new light. The album’s 12 tracks are a satisfying display of their combined powers that rattle in your chest, from the nocturnal pleasure of “Saltwater” to the radiant funk of “The Darkest Part.” —_NH_

![Image 16: camp cope record](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-camp-cope-run-for-cover-records.jpeg)

Run For Cover Records

Camp Cope – _Running with the Hurricane_

There is still so much to be angry about, but on their third record, [**Camp Cope**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/camp-cope/) choose to replace the fury of their past with tender vulnerability. Folk-rock and fresh pop-country melodies accompany the feeling that the Australian trio have assembled newfound self-acceptance. Singer Georgia Maq treats emotions gently and never takes herself too seriously. She swallows her pride to double text a crush or forgives someone before they’ve even apologized. _Running with the Hurricane_ reminds us that there is always room for reinvention. As Maq declares on the title track, “The only way out is up.” —_Natalia Barr_

![Image 17: charli xcx crash](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-charli-atlantic-records.jpeg)

Atlantic Records

Charli XCX – _CRASH_

Throughout the promo of _CRASH_, hyperpop princess [**Charli XCX**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/charli-xcx/) joked that it was her "major label sell-out record" and that she was ready to sell her soul to the industry. It was all very cheeky, coming from the alt-pop experimenter — and it ended up feeding into the record in fascinating ways. _CRASH_ as a whole sounds like a love letter from one of pop's brightest and most attentive students, infusing her future-minded production with '80s disco and Y2K bubblegum elements. But that's just Charli, baby: an innovator who's always been a main pop girl at heart, and thank goodness for that. —_SB_

![Image 18: demi holy fvck](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-demi-island-records.jpeg)

Island Records

Demi Lovato – _HOLY FVCK_

After years of releasing R&B-tinged power ballads and pop records, [**Demi Lovato**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/demi-lovato/) returned to her rock roots with [_HOLY FVCK_](https://www.altpress.com/demi-lovato-holy-fvck-interview/)_._ Her eighth studio album was flanked by hard-rock choruses and pop-punk anthems, brimming with religious imagery and sex. But the anchor of the record has been the song "29," a defiant rock ballad that grapples with consent. For Lovato and her fans, _HOLY FVCK_ is a new beginning and a return to form. —_IK_

RCA Records

Steve Lacy – _Gemini Rights_

Inspired by a bad breakup, [**Steve Lacy**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/steve-lacy/)’s second record is confident and grandiose, full of rich fusions of funk, jazz and R&B. Ditching the GarageBand solo ventures of his debut, _Gemini Rights_’ collaborative fanfare makes heartbreak sound enticing. The viral, chart-topping earworm “Bad Habit” is a perfect example. Its optimistic guitar rifts contrast Lacy’s beseeching vocals as he pines for someone toxic. Filled with equal parts empathy and desperation, _Gemini Rights_ is a too-relatable, all-consuming cocktail. —_MCG_

![Image 50: Sudan Archives album](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-sudan-stones-throw-records.jpeg)

Stones Throw Records

Sudan Archives – _Natural Brown Prom Queen_

[**Sudan Archives**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/sudan-archives/) conjures magic with a flick of her violin bow. From the jump, her spectacular sophomore album, _Natural Brown Prom Queen_, puts you under a spell, offering an excursion through many of the things that Archives succeeds at so well — boundless creativity, maximalism, and love and precision for her craft. Through the record’s 18 tracks, Archives exudes confidence and charisma at every turn as she sings of home, sexuality, and Blackness. It’s the ultimate hallucinogenic soundtrack for the prom you might’ve missed out on. —_NH_

![Image 51: sza sos](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-sza-top-dawg-entertainment-and-rca-records.jpeg)

Top Dawg Entertainment/RCA Records

SZA – _SOS_

[**SZA**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/sza/) still gets it. On her debut, the singer intimately described insecurities without any hint of shame or secrecy. Her new album, _SOS_, reminds us that those intrusive anxieties never truly disappear, but maturity makes them easier to swallow. Across 23 tracks, there is no limit to the shapes SZA’s voice can take. She soars on the pop-punk-driven “F2F,” creeps alongside Phoebe Bridgers on “Ghost in the Machine,” and destroys and conquers on the opening track. “And all the petty shit aside/All the funny shit aside/I just want what’s mine,” she asserts. SZA, it’s all yours. —_NB_

![Image 52](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-taylor-republic-records.jpeg)

Republic Records

Taylor Swift – _Midnights_

[**Taylor Swift**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/taylor-swift/) is a master of reinvention, crafting eras, personas, and expertly curating genres throughout her _oeuvre_. You could say, she's somewhat of a mastermind. On her 10th studio album, [_Midnights_](https://www.altpress.com/taylor-swift-midnights-review/), she proves that, setting an atmosphere of late nights drenched in regret, drinks, and self-loathing. Throughout the album's 13 songs (and eight bonus tracks), Swift uses synth-pop teeming with reverb, delicate balladry, and catchy pop hooks to deliver some of her most soul-baring lines, with a smile and a wink. _—IK_

![Image 53: dawn fm](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-weeknd-xo-republic-records.jpeg)

XO/Republic Records

The Weeknd – _Dawn FM_

Leave it to forever sad boy [**the Weeknd**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/the-weeknd/) to make a concept album that plays out like the radio show you hear en route to the afterlife — and also make it an absolute banger. While the concept might sound bleak, it's the R&B hitmaker at his most playful, reuniting with frequent collaborator Daniel Lopatin of Oneohtrix Point Never for many tracks to create a glittery, retro-pop universe. If the '80s-inspired dance-pop synths on "Take My Breath" are what purgatory sounds like, dancing until you're dead doesn't sound bad at all. —_SB_

![Image 54: wet leg album](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-wet-leg-domino.jpeg)

Domino Records

Wet Leg – _Wet Leg_

Your mid-to-late 20s can be a weird time; when some friends are getting married, you might still feel like you were 21 just yesterday, and can't fathom what's next. So bless Rhian Teasdale and Hester Chambers of the Isle of Wight-based indie group [**Wet Leg**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/wet-leg/) for uniting two years ago to write about all of those feelings — and doing it in the most lively, post-punk way. From parties where the vibes feel off to being in love to rejecting less than what they deserve and craving something more, [_Wet Leg_](https://www.altpress.com/wet-leg-interview-issue-402/) dives into it all, with a delightful helping of arty arrangements, hooks, and silly one-liners. You can tell they're having fun, and it's a reminder at how fruitful life can be when you feel it all and take it as it comes. —_SB_

![Image 55: Weyes Blood album](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-weyes-blood-supbop.jpeg)

Sub Pop

Weyes Blood – _And in the Darkness, Hearts Aglow_

Natalie Mering, who performs as [**Weyes Blood**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/weyes-blood/), has called her latest album [_And in the Darkness, Hearts Aglow_](https://www.altpress.com/weyes-blood-and-in-the-darkness-hearts-aglow-interview/) a thematic follow-up to 2019's _Titanic Rising_ — with that album sensing catastrophe was in the air, and _AITDHA_ reporting what it's like in the thick of it. Even as Weyes Blood sings of isolation, societal collapse, and disastrous heartbreak, there's a glimmer of optimism, relayed in her vivid lyricism and atmospheric, chamber-pop melodies. As she sings on "God Turn Me Into a Flower," there's beauty and, more importantly, hope to be found in vulnerability. Those sentiments shine through, and even the softest of moments are stunners. —_SB_

![Image 56: willow album](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-willow-msftsmusic-roc-nation-records.jpg)

Msftsmusic/Roc Nation

WILLOW – _COPINGMECHANISM_

You cannot deny that [**WILLOW**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/willow-smith/) released one of the best rock albums of 2022, which is sure to be looked at as a blueprint to study for years to come. With her fifth studio album, [_<COPINGMECHANISM>_](https://www.altpress.com/willow-influences-album-avril-lavigne-cover-story/), it seems WILLOW experienced a renewed sense of musical freedom, which includes an embrace of hard-rock and nü-metal elements that allows the vocal powerhouse to shine on every front. Whether it’s heavy arena bangers (“ur a <stranger>”) or upbeat pop rock (“hover like a GODDESS,” “curious/furious”), WILLOW avoids filler and puts heart, soul, and intentionality behind every track. —_AD_

![Image 57: wonder years album](https://media.altpress.com/fkdgxpscnt/uploads/2022/12/09/attachment-wonder-years-the-loneliest-place-on-earth-and-hopeless-records.jpeg)

The Loneliest Place on Earth/Hopeless Records

The Wonder Years – _The Hum Goes on Forever_

After a series of marriages, births, tragedies, and a pandemic, [**the Wonder Years**](https://www.altpress.com/tags/the-wonder-years/) had more than enough material for their seventh album, [_The Hum Goes on Forever_](https://www.altpress.com/the-wonder-years-the-hum-goes-on-forever-interview/). The record is largely a return to their classic sound, albeit with newfound wisdom that's applied brilliantly (“Wyatt’s Song (Your Name),” “Old Friends Like Lost Teeth”). Though the record touches on topics of loss and societal collapse, it comes to a heartfelt conclusion. “You’re The Reason I Don’t Want the World to End” makes peace with madness and serves as a touching reminder that sometimes all we all need to do is lean on our loved ones whenever the world feels like a scary place. —_AD_

Album review: Pinkshift – Love Me Forever
=========================================

Hotly-tipped pop-punk n00bs Pinkshift fulfil their promise on banging debut full-length…

![Image 1: Album review: Pinkshift – Love Me Forever](https://images.kerrangcdn.com/images/2022/10/PINKSHIFT-WEB-SLEEVE-2022.jpg?auto=compress&fit=max&w=3840)

October 21, 2022

Words:

Nick Ruskell

The way [Pinkshift](https://www.kerrang.com/artists/pinkshift) tell it, their families don’t quite get why they’re doing what they’re doing. Having started while the members were in college, it was only meant to be a passing thing. Singer Ashrita Kumar and drummer Myron Houngbedji had their sights set on medical school, while guitarist Paul Vallejo was lining up to train in engineering. When their single i’m gonna tell my therapist on you suddenly exploded, all that went on the back burner. Their parents were puzzled.

Love Me Forever may just make them understand what’s going on here. Already one of the most hotly-tipped pop-punk bands of the past 10 years, it’s a debut that’s accomplished and wise beyond Pinkshift’s years (especially considering the relatively small amount of touring they’ve done). Those already in the know will have already witnessed this in the lead up to the album thanks to the massive i’m not crying you’re crying and nothing (in my head), which open things with an effervescent one-two of sugar-rush melody and electric energy. Happily, though putting strong feet forward, the rest of Love Me Forever hits just the same way.

In fact, Pinkshift do a lot more here than banging pop-punk. cherry (we’re all gonna die) comes on like [Turnstile](https://www.kerrang.com/artists/turnstile) with bigger choruses, a trick repeated on the riffy the kids aren’t alright. Cinderella takes a softer, more anthemic approach, before BURN THE WITCH explodes with a fighty power. It’s sharp, skilful and bristling with infectious energy. That they release something verging on aggression at times is very welcome as well.

Love Me Forever is a bold first proper kick from a band already brimming with promise. It announces Pinkshift as an already killer band, while also setting them up for future glory. Medical school’s loss is very much music’s gain.

**Verdict: 4/5**

**For fans of: [Paramore](https://www.kerrang.com/artists/paramore), Turnstile, [Marmozets](https://www.kerrang.com/artists/marmozets)**

Leigh Ann Rogers

One of the most exciting new bands in the scene today, [Pinkshift](https://www.kerrang.com/artists/pinkshift/) are continuing to build on their already impressive momentum with the announcement of their debut album Love Me Forever.

The highly-anticipated LP is due out on October 21 via Hopeless Records, with new single – and album opener – i’m not crying, you’re crying out now (watch the lyric video below).

Of that particular tune, vocalist Ashrita Kumar explains that it’s “the one song on the record that I didn’t start with a particular direction, just raw and unfiltered emotion.

“As the first song on Love Me Forever, it kicks the record off with a panicked denial – an immediately attacking response to the question of ‘Are you okay?’ untrusting and doubtful of the intent and sincerity of that question.”

The single follows previous releases “nothing (in my head)” and ‘i’m not crying, you’re crying. _Love Me Forever_, was recorded by [Will Yip](https://northerntransmissions.com/quicksand-stay-strong-and-contemporary/) ([Turnstile](https://northerntransmissions.com/turnstile-drop-new-heart-design-video/), [Mannequin Pussy](https://northerntransmissions.com/mannequin-pussy-perfect/), [Tigers Jaw](https://northerntransmissions.com/escape-plan-by-tigers-jaw/)) and drops on October 21st via Hopeless Records.

“”Get Out” is an anthem to be utilized to take space where it’s not inherently given to us. “It’s a blatant attack against the white supremacist and patriarchal colonizers of our bodies, homes, and ways of life, and it’s an expression of pure and unapologetic rage that stands in defense of our autonomy.” Says singer Ashrita Kumar.

### Pinkshift

#### _Love Me Forever_

##### Hopeless

Oct 24, 2022 [Web Exclusive](https://www.undertheradarmag.com/issues/webexclusive) By Caleb Campbell

_Love Me Forever_, the debut record from Baltimore punks [Pinkshift](https://undertheradarmag.com/artists/pinkshift) opens with a roar: “I’m so sorry that you’re seeing me this way,” apologizes lead singer Ashrita Kumar just before the band tears in with all of the force of a bulldozer. That searing energy and visceral vulnerability are the two twin hearts of the band’s debut, a record that is both pummelling and purposeful.

Kumar spits, snarls, and soars as guitarist Paul Vallejo crafts whirlwind riffs and Myron Houngbedji’s muscular drumming sets the record’s breakneck pace. Through nearly the entire LP, the band conjure the cathartic magic of punk, playing so fast and loud they should seemingly come apart at the seams.

All along, the band walk a fraying edge between frenzied confessions and righteous fury. They explore the nihilism of a generation growing up with an uncertain future, the wounds of trauma and abuse, and the alienation of living unapologetically in a hostile world. Yet, they emerge at the other end unbowed, unbroken, and powerful. The resulting record is a stellar punk debut, claiming Pinkshift’s spot among the genre’s next generation, a future that is both more inclusive and angrier than ever. ([www.pinkshiftmd.com](http://www.pinkshiftmd.com/))

================================================================

Our October CoSigns unleash a thrilling debut

Today’s mainstream social media stars evoke 2000s Myspace royalty; Megan Fox is engaged to a rapper-turned-rock star; Travis Barker is married to a Kardashian; and, oh yeah, Tom DeLonge re-joined Blink-182 — have you heard that pop punk is back? It all sounds unlikely, but perhaps even more surprising than the evolution of the genre into 2022 is the rise of [Pinkshift](https://consequence.net/artist/pinkshift/), a Baltimore trio who met at Johns Hopkins University, bonded over a shared love of My Chemical Romance, and dropped their respective STEM career paths in favor of fucking shit up.

Pinkshift, our [CoSign for October 2022](https://consequence.net/2022/10/pinkshift-love-me-forever-artist-of-the-month-interview/), became hotshots overnight in August 2020 with their viral breakout single “I’m Gonna Tell My Therapist On You,” which encapsulates many of the band’s biggest strengths — Paul Vallejo’s chugging guitar, Myron Houngbedji’s breakneck beats, and, most crucially, Ashrita Kumar’s biting vocals.

Pinkshift then preceded their debut album [_Love Me Forever_](https://consequence.net/2022/07/pinkshift-love-me-forever-im-not-crying-youre-crying-stream/) (out Friday, October 21st) with its opening track, the single “i’m not crying, you’re crying” — a barrage of racing drums and nimble riffs. “I’m so sorry that you’re seeing me this way,” Kumar sings in its first lines, as if scrambling to catch their cool again. Though Pinkshift toy with expressions of tongue-in-cheek regret and conciliatory self-preservation, what’s to come on the rest of the record is hardly apologetic.

Advertisement

Empowerment is a driving force behind the ethos of Pinkshift, and that vigor is felt in _Love Me Forever_’s musings on fraught romances. Take “Trust Fall,” where Kumar airs their grievances from an abusive relationship. “Now I’m a shell of who I was/ So undesirable/ Walking on eggshells just because,” they sing. Later, on the thrashing, muscular “Cinderella,” Kumar envisions setting their brain ablaze to eviscerate all memories of their betrayer: “Let my ashes fall so I won’t ever feel anything again.”

Especially backed by the razor-sharp production of punk studio wiz Will Yip (Turnstile, Mannequin Pussy, The Wonder Years), these moments embody the well-worn formula that makes pop-punk so cathartic for the inconsolable.

Though _Love Me Forever_ does tend to lean on tropes of indulgent angst, it also sees Pinkshift big on broader societal topics. “BURN THE WITCH” reworks infamous 17th-century prosecutions into an analysis of groupthink and its disproportionate maliciousness towards women. “What if we peeled away her skin/ Off of her bones and she’d reveal herself a monster within/ And then we’ve won and we can all go home and celebrate in sin,” Kumar sings, before delivering one of the album’s best one-liners In the chorus: “You’ve got two feet, now won’t you stand for something?”

Advertisement

Maybe the most haunting message that lies behind _Love Me Forever_, however, is the notion that the “forever” Pinkshift speak of is unpredictable: How does one prepare when disaster feels imminent, yet undefined? The album attempts to grapple with a futile reality at a time when societal collapse is in the air, and though Kumar’s protests can feel on the nose at times — “The world is ending all the time and I don’t think I can take it,” goes one such example in “the kids aren’t all right” — _Love Me Forever_ is also peppered with subtly powerful admissions of anguish.

“What is it like when you can sleep with no alarm?” Kumar speculates on the startlingly spare piano ballad “in a breath.” Who knows when we’ll find out, but in the meantime, Pinkshift have created a useful companion for the world’s downfall.

**Essential Tracks:**“i’m not crying you’re crying,” “trust fall,” “let me drown”
